title: Tech Note: NT Localization
author: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon
featured_technology: 4D Script Manager systems (smRoman, smJapanese, smArabic, smCyrillic, smEastEurRoman)
Mac to ISO / ISO to Mac commands
FONT, FONT SIZE, FONT STYLE commands

historical_commentary.text: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon (4D QA Manager) explains, in considerable depth, how 4D's classic engine handled Script Manager-based foreign-language systems (Roman vs. non-Roman scripts), how TRIC resources drove sorting/searching, how the 'MapC' resource translated characters between Mac and Windows, and how style sheets were the recommended way to adapt fonts for Central European, Asian, and Arabic markets. This entire code-page/TRIC/Script-Manager approach to internationalization is obsolete: 4D introduced native Unicode text handling starting around 4D v11 SQL (2007), which eliminated the need for platform-specific script managers, MapC translation tables, and manual TRIC resource selection for most modern development. The note is now useful only as a historical record of pre-Unicode 4D internals.
related_updates: 4D introduced native Unicode text support beginning around 4D v11 SQL (~2007), superseding Script Manager/TRIC/MapC-based localization
Windows NT itself is long obsolete, superseded by many subsequent Windows releases
4D's style sheets feature (recommended in this note for font/localization handling) remains part of the product today
